newsitem.title: FRANCE: Large Egyptian contract underpins French wheat.
newsitem.headline: Large Egyptian contract underpins French wheat.

text.p: French wheat prices rose on Monday on Sunday's news of a large surprise sale of French soft wheat to Egypt, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen for September-December delivery was bid at 885 francs per tonne, up 10 francs from Friday. But sellers were holding out, offering their wheat at 890-900 francs per tonne.

Egypt had initially sought 50,000 tonnes of French wheat but ended up buying 450,000 tonnes of French soft red wheat over the weekend at prices ranging from $163.90 to $167 per tonne, fob, for loading in October and November.
Traders described the selling prices as very low, particularly when compared to the sale some two weeks ago of 200,000 tonnes of French wheat to Egypt at $178 a tonne fob.
"We knew Egypt wanted to buy more (than 50,000 tonnes) but we did not expect 450,000 tonnes," one trader said.

Further export business may also be in the pipeline as Morocco is expected to tender on September 18 for the purchase of 35,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat for shipment in the first half of October, dealers said.
